correctness.rationale: For equal decks, the fixed zero count and the counts 011=3a+b and 110=c+3d force the integral shift (-t,3t,-3t,t). The numbers of zeros preceding the three ones change by (-t,2t,-t), so the change in the sum of their binomial coefficients choose 2 is t(b-c+3t). The corresponding suffix-zero count 100 has the same change; the sum of the three two-zero counts is fixed, so 010 changes by minus twice that amount. The other five deck entries are fixed along the shift. The nonzero root therefore gives exactly the stated involution when the gaps are nonnegative integers, not merely a candidate. Choosing b>c gives b=c+3s, d=s+e, and n=3+a+e+2c+4s, proving the pair series and the singleton/doubleton formulas. The order-four pole at 1 gives n^3/48, with lower-order contributions at the other roots of unity; the mate proportion tends to 1/4.
residual_risks: The separate finite enumeration is a check, not the all-length proof or an audit of auxiliary four-deck claims.
